hints: Focus on oxidation numbers first, since this is disproportionation the same nitrogen in HNO2 must both go up and go down.
Work out that N is +3 in HNO2, +5 in HNO3 and +2 in NO, so oxidation loses 2 electrons while reduction gains only 1.
Balance the electrons gained and lost to find the ratio of HNO3 to NO, then use nitrogen balance to find how many HNO2 you started with.
walkthrough:
**Find oxidation number of nitrogen in each species**

Nitrogen is the only element oxidised or reduced, so track it carefully. Use the rule H is +1 and O is -2.

$$\text{In HNO}_2: +1 + N + 2(-2) = 0 \text{ so } N = +3$$
$$\text{In HNO}_3: +1 + N + 3(-2) = 0 \text{ so } N = +5$$
$$\text{In NO}: N + (-2) = 0 \text{ so } N = +2$$

**Identify oxidation and reduction and balance electrons**

$N(+3)$ to $N(+5)$ is oxidation, it loses 2 electrons. $N(+3)$ to $N(+2)$ is reduction, it gains 1 electron.

$$\text{oxidation: HNO}_2 \rightarrow \text{HNO}_3 + 2e^-$$
$$\text{reduction: HNO}_2 + e^- \rightarrow \text{NO}$$
To make electrons lost equal electrons gained, you need two reductions for every one oxidation. So U : V must be 1 : 2.

**Balance nitrogen atoms to find W**

Total N on the right is $U + V = 1 + 2 = 3$. All that nitrogen must come from $\text{HNO}_2$ on the left, so $W = 3$.

$$3\text{HNO}_2 \rightarrow \text{HNO}_3 + 2\text{NO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This gives $W = 3$, $U = 1$, $V = 2$, with H and O balanced by water.

options.A: 2, 1, 1 would balance nitrogen atoms but not electrons. One oxidation loses 2 electrons but one reduction gains only 1, so charge and electrons are not balanced.
options.B: 3, 1, 2 correctly balances both atoms and electrons. One N(+3) is oxidised to N(+5) losing 2 electrons, and two N(+3) are reduced to N(+2) gaining 2 electrons in total.
options.C: 5, 3, 2 balances nitrogen atoms (5 = 3 + 2) but gives the wrong electron ratio. Three oxidations would lose 6 electrons while two reductions gain only 2 electrons.
options.D: 5, 1, 4 balances nitrogen atoms (5 = 1 + 4) but reverses the electron logic. One oxidation loses 2 electrons while four reductions would gain 4 electrons, so electrons do not balance.
